name: Environmental movement
summary: The environmental movement is the broad coalition of citizens and organizations that campaign to protect the natural environment from pollution, resource exploitation and species loss. Its sources stress the value of nature, government regulation of pollution, international action on climate, population and nuclear dangers, and sustainability for future generations. Beyond ecology it has little doctrine, so most economic and social questions are unanswered.
scope: The modern environmental movement as its defining reference works describe it: its history from the conservation writings of Muir and Leopold through Carson, Earth Day 1970 and the global climate agenda, with Leopold's land ethic and the Brundtland report as texts the sources tie to it. Individual organizations and green parties are other subjects.
